priorities.finding: Prioritize request-context features. Training-only screening shows the only positive primary lift (+0.0022), with positive lift on 3 of 4 days, and the official experiment improves primary from 0.5885 to 0.6029 while achieving GAUC 0.6689. The warm-user-and-item GAUC of 0.6312 and cold-user GAUC of 0.6536 indicate useful within-user ranking evidence rather than classification-only gain.
priorities.recommended_action: Spend the next budget unit on one confirmatory run retaining tab, hour, and weekday, with the same architecture and temporal split. Stop further expansion if the confirmatory primary or GAUC does not improve.

priorities.finding: Treat post-score diagnostics as robustness targets, not as evidence to add new features. Top-five quality is especially weak in tab 8 and tab 0, while tab 8 also has GAUC 0.3519; hour 3 has the weakest hourly GAUC at 0.5318. These weaknesses are not explained by the strong global GAUC alone.
priorities.recommended_action: In the confirmatory run, report GAUC and nDCG@5 separately by tab and hour, and inspect whether request-context interactions improve these slices without sacrificing aggregate within-user ranking.

avoid: Reject user-profile, historical user-author affinity, upload-recency, content-duration, item-metadata, historical-author-response, and historical-item-response groups based on their negative training-only primary lifts; do not spend additional budget on them.
Do not use current-impression outcomes or aggregate snapshots lacking impression-time availability timestamps; they are leakage risks and must remain excluded from ranking inputs.
Do not treat user_positive_count zero or other post-score validation segments as deployable features; they use retrospective validation labels and are diagnostic only.
metric_diagnosis: The experiment provides credible but modest ranking evidence: global GAUC is 0.6689 and primary is 0.6029, with an observed primary gain of 0.0144 versus the prior experiment, exceeding the 0.002 predicted gain. GAUC supports broad within-user ordering quality, while top-five metrics reveal concentrated weaknesses, notably tab 8 (nDCG@5 0.0263, primary 0.1891) and the zero-positive validation slice (nDCG@5 0, primary 0.25). Because segment diagnostics are official-validation slices rather than independent test estimates, apply the strict early-stop rule after one confirmatory request-context run rather than launching broad feature exploration.
